headline: 839 hospitalised in 24 hours as 5 more die of dengue
summary: The total death toll has risen to 82, with nearly 29,000 cases recorded so far this year, according to the DGHS.
details: At least five dengue patients died and 839 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am today, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the deaths, three were reported in Dhaka South City Corporation, and one each in Dhaka and Mymensingh divisions.
With these latest figures, the total number of dengue deaths in the country has risen to 82, while total cases have reached 28,929.
Currently, 1,951 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at various hospitals across the country.

headline: Brazil football delegation inspects National Stadium for potential match
summary: A five-member team from the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) visited Dhaka to assess the venue for a future match against Bangladesh or as a neutral site.
details: A five-member delegation from the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) inspected the National Stadium in Dhaka on Sunday to assess its suitability for a match against Bangladesh or as a neutral venue.
Led by Sergio Dimas de Oliveira, general supervisor of the men’s national team, the team spent 45 minutes reviewing the newly laid pitch, dressing rooms, galleries, and other facilities.
The visit occurred after the delegation landed in Dhaka from Kolkata, where they had previously inspected the Salt Lake Stadium ahead of Brazil’s friendly against India in October.
BFF executive committee member Iqbal Hossain stated that the CBF indicated the stadium could be used for a future match against Bangladesh or as a neutral venue.
Hossain noted that ground preparations are ongoing and may take another two weeks to complete, adding that the delegation may visit again if necessary.
The inspection included a review of the ground's watering and sewerage systems before the team visited the dressing rooms and galleries.
caption:
Could Brazil be coming to Dhaka? 🇧🇷

A delegation from the Brazilian Football Confederation just inspected the National Stadium.

A five-member delegation from the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) inspected the National Stadium in Dhaka on Sunday to assess its suitability for a match against Bangladesh or as a neutral venue.

Led by Sergio Dimas de Oliveira, general supervisor of the men’s national team, the team spent 45 minutes reviewing the newly laid pitch, dressing rooms, galleries, and other facilities.

The visit occurred after the delegation landed in Dhaka from Kolkata, where they had previously inspected the Salt Lake Stadium ahead of Brazil’s friendly against India in October.

BFF executive committee member Iqbal Hossain stated that the CBF indicated the stadium could be used for a future match against Bangladesh or as a neutral venue.

Hossain noted that ground preparations are ongoing and may take another two weeks to complete, adding that the delegation may visit again if necessary.

The inspection included a review of the ground's watering and sewerage systems before the team visited the dressing rooms and galleries.
